prompt: Which workspace has the channel where the postmortem write-up for the checkout latency incident was posted?
binding_note: The workspace is identified transitively: WORKSPACE(teams.team_id) = CONVERSATION.team_id, and the conversation must contain a MESSAGE whose text is the posted postmortem for the checkout latency incident. Two channels in two different workspaces both carry a matching postmortem message, so the request resolves to two distinct candidate workspaces rather than one.

roles.reason: One candidate workspace whose channel holds a matching checkout-latency postmortem.

roles.facts: T02NOVA (Nova Robotics), a second workspace the acting user also belongs to, contains channel ops-incidents.
roles.reason: Second candidate workspace whose channel holds a matching checkout-latency postmortem.

roles.facts: Channel core-infra (C_INFRA), team_id=T01WORKSPACE, actor is a member.
roles.reason: Supplies the workspace link for the matching message in workspace_infra.

roles.facts: Channel ops-incidents (C_NOVA_OPS), team_id=T02NOVA, actor is also a member.
roles.reason: Supplies the workspace link for the matching message in workspace_nova.

roles.facts: Priya posts in core-infra: 'Postmortem posted: checkout latency incident from last Tuesday — root cause traced to connection pool exhaustion under peak load.'
roles.reason: Directly matches the requested postmortem content and binds to workspace_infra via its channel.

roles.facts: Jordan Lee posts in ops-incidents: 'Postmortem posted: checkout latency incident from last Tuesday — root cause was a stale Redis cache serving expired pricing data.'
roles.reason: Also matches the requested postmortem content and binds to workspace_nova via its channel.

roles.facts: Kenji posts in product-growth: 'Postmortem posted: Tokyo launch activation incident — root cause traced to CDN misrouting through Singapore.'
roles.reason: Uses the same 'postmortem posted' phrasing but concerns a different incident (activation/CDN, not checkout latency), so it must not be treated as a match.

roles.facts: Existing core-infra thread about GPU memory pressure and OOM kills, unrelated to checkout latency.
roles.reason: Same channel/workspace as a true match but wrong topic; shows the workspace alone isn't sufficient without the specific postmortem message.

roles.facts: Existing product-growth thread discussing Tokyo p95 latency fixes without ever framing it as a 'postmortem posted' for checkout latency.
roles.reason: Topically adjacent (latency) but neither a postmortem nor about checkout, so it does not satisfy the identifying condition.

obligations.name: postmortem_workspace
obligations.description: Select the workspace(s) whose channel contains the message announcing the checkout latency incident postmortem; report which workspace(s) that is.
obligations.scope: workspaces reachable through channels the acting user is a member of

task_spec.text: Identify which workspace hosts the channel where the checkout latency incident postmortem was posted, and report the workspace.

access_plan: List the acting user's own conversation memberships (channel_members / users.conversations) to obtain the bounded set of channels the user can see across any workspaces they belong to; for each channel, pull message history (conversations.history / search.messages) looking for a message whose text announces a posted postmortem for the checkout latency incident; each matching message's channel carries a team_id that identifies its workspace. Do not rely on any workspace-name lookup or full workspace enumeration, since neither is exposed.
